Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 8055 of 2023
Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Subir Lal,Swetashwa Agarwal
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri S.B. Maurya-Ist, learned Aga for the State apprised the Court that he has received instructions
in the present matter, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be disposed of on
merit.
2. Heard Sri Swetashwa Agarwal, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri S.B. Maurya-Ist, learned
A.G.A. for the State.

3.  The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 02 of 2019, under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 120-B IPC, Police Station Kalyanpur,
District West Commissionerate Kanpur Nagar, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and 8 others on 02.01.2019 and according to the FIR, in the year 1997 applicant was posted as Senior Manager in UPSIDC, Kanpur Pradeep Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62910374/
1 and he was asked to prepare MoU between UPSIDC and Ansals Housing and Construction Limited and thereafter he prepared the MoU and subsequently the same was executed.

entities.text: UPSIDC, Kanpur Pradeep Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. It is further mention in the FIR that subsequently it came to know that the MoU was prepared on Rs.50 Stamp and it was not registered and thereafter on 16.01.2015 Assistant Commissioner Stamp passed an order against the Ansals Construction Limited that there were a deficiency of the stamp of more than 3 crore, therefore, applicant and others committed offence of cheating, forgery and misappropriation.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits on the basis of false allegation applicant has been made accused in the present case.
He further submits that applicant was the person who only prepared the MoU, he neither signed the same nor he was having any authority to execute the same.

He further submit, subsequently when an order was passed by the Assistant Commissioner Stamp with regard to the insufficiency of the Stamp duty of more than 3 crore then a revision was filed by the Ansals Construction Limited before Board of Revenue Circuit Bench Meerut, which was ultimately allowed on 22.04.2015 and order dated 16.01.2015 passed by Assistant Commissioner Stamp was set aside.

entities.text: Board of Revenue Circuit Bench Meerut
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He further submits both the orders passed by the Assistant Commissioner Stamp and Board of Revenue have been annexed along with the instant anticipatory bail application.

He further submit,
however, in the FIR there is a mention of order dated 16.01.2015 passed by the Assistant Commissioner Stamp but there is no disclosure of the order passed by Board of Revenue dated 22.04.2015.
Therefore, FIR of the present case was lodged by concealing the material facts available on record.

7. He further submits against the order dated 22.04.2015 passed by Board of Revenue, the State Government preferred a Writ C No.54660 of 2015 in which, however, notices were issued but no interim order could be passed in favour of the State Government and writ filed by the State Government is still pending.

He further submits that applicant is about 71 years old person and he has already taken VRS in the year 2006 and FIR in the present case was lodged after more than 2 decade and it is a matter in which arrest of the applicant is not required.

He placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court inSiddharth Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another (2022) 1 SCC 676 and submitted if there is no need of arrest then personal liberty of a person should be protected and in such matter the anticipatory bail application should be allowed.

entities.text: inSiddharth Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another (2022) 1 SCC 676
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. He further submit, however, apart from the present case applicant is also having criminal antecedent of a case under Section 409 IPC but that case also arose from the same dispute and a FIR was lodged against the applicant under Section 379 IPC in the year 2011 and during investigation which continued upto 8 years it was found that the MoU allotment file was misplaced and applicant did not even tried to search it and, after investigation, charge-sheet was filed against the applicant in that case under Section 409 IPC.

He further submits in that case applicant has already been released on anticipatory bail by this Court and anticipatory bail order dated 23.03.2022 passed by this Court has been annexed as Annexure No.2 to the affidavit.
9. He further submits that, therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case applicant should be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

2 10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned A.G.A. however, opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submitted that applicant with the connivance of the Ansals Constructions Limited prepared the MoU on the stamp paper of Rs.50 and without registration of the MoU the same was executed and therefore due to the conduct of the applicant State Government suffered a loss of more than 3 crores, but he could not dispute the fact that the order dated 16.01.2015 passed by the Assistant Commissioner Stamp for deficiency of the stamp duty has been set aside by the Board of Revenue Circuit Bench Meerut on 22.04.2015 and till date the order passed by the Board of Revenue could not be either stayed or set aside at any higher forum including this Court.

entities.text: Board of Revenue Circuit Bench Meerut
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, learned A.G.A submitted that against the order passed by the Board of Revenue, State filed Writ C which is still pending, but he fairly conceaded in Writ C No.54660 of 2015, no interim order could be obtained by the State.
He further could not dispute the fact that applicant is more than 70 years and he has already taken VRS and FIR of the present case was lodged after more than 2 decades.

However, he submitted that apart from the present case applicant is also having criminal antecedents of Sections 409 IPC but again he could not dispute the fact that in that case applicant is already on anticipatory bail.
11. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

12. From the record it reflects that applicant in the year 1997 posted as Senior Manager in UPSIDC Kanpur and he prepared the MoU which was subsequently executed between UPSIDC and Ansals Constructiions and it appears that the MoU was prepared on Rs.50 stamp paper and on 16.01.2015 Assistant Commissioner Stamp found that the alleged MoU ought to be registered and therefore without paying proper stamp duty it has been executed and a penalty of more than one crore along with stamp deficiency of more than three crore have been imposed upon the Ansals Construction Limited.

Record further reveals that against the order dated 16.01.2015 Ansals Constructions preferred revision before Board of Revenue Circuit Bench Meerut and on 22.04.2015 Board of Revenue was pleased to set aside the order dated 16.01.2015 passed by the Assistant Commissioner Stamp.

entities.text: Board of Revenue Circuit Bench Meerut
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Record further suggests that, however, against the order dated 22.04.2015 passed by the Board of Revenue Circuit Bench Meerut, State filed a Writ C No.54660 of 2015 before this court and in that matter notices were issued but no interim order could be passed in favour of the State and writ filed by the State is still pending.

entities.text: Board of Revenue Circuit Bench Meerut
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, the order dated 22.04.2015 passed by the Board of Revenue is till intact.

13. Further, from perusal of the FIR, it appears that FIR of the present case was lodged on 02.01.2019 after the order dated 16.01.2015 passed by the Assistant Commissioner Stamp and order date 22.04.2015 passed by Board of Revenue and it was lodged by Inspector C.B.C.I.D, but while lodging the same it could not be noticed that the order dated 16.01.2015 has already been set aside by the Board of Revenue in revision on 22.04.2015.
Further the FIR of the present case was lodged after more than 20 years, further applicant is more than 70 years old and he has already taken VRS from the service in the year 2006.

The Apex Court in the case of Siddharth Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another (2022) 1 SCC 676 categorically stated that personal liberty of the person provided under Article 21 is the most cherished fundamental right provided in the Constitution of India and even if there is power of arrest but if there is no need of arrest then an accused should not be arrested and he should be granted pre arrest bail.

sentences.text: Considering the nature of allegation, and the age of the applicant, this Court is of the view that the arrest of the applicant does not appear to be necessary.

15. Further, however, apart from the present case applicant is also having criminal history of one another case under Section 409 IPC but that case also arose from the present dispute and it appears that as per allegation the MoU allotment file was misplaced from the applicant and it appears that this Court has already enlarged the applicant on anticipatory bail in that case and order of the same is annexed as Annexure -2 to the affidavit.
16.
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
17. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

20. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
